attempts.raw_response: The court heard that Catt had concealed her pregnancy from her husband and family members, having previously hidden an earlier pregnancy before placing that child for adoption. Prosecutors told jurors that she had researched methods of terminating pregnancies online in the weeks before the birth. When questioned by police, Catt maintained she could not remember where she had buried the infant, despite extensive searches of areas she was known to frequent. The prosecution described her demeanour throughout the investigation as cold and calculated, arguing she had shown no remorse for her actions. Her defence team argued she had suffered significant mental health difficulties and had acted in a state of acute psychological distress. The judge remanded her in custody ahead of sentencing, telling the court that the seriousness of the offence warranted immediate imprisonment.

pair.human_continuation: She later had a termination with the agreement of her husband, tried to terminate another pregnancy but missed the legal limit and concealed another pregnancy from her husband before the child's birth. Mr Justice Cooke said Catt had robbed the baby of the life it was about to have and said the seriousness of the crime lay between manslaughter and murder. Sentencing, the judge told Catt she clearly thought the man with whom she was having an affair was the father and she had shown no remorse. Ch Insp Kerrin Smith, who led the North Yorkshire Police investigation, said the case was "unusual, disturbing and very complicated". Catt had proved to be "more than capable of being extremely deceitful in her actions", said Ch Insp Smith.
